fable-fusion-27b.note: Community merge (DavidAU Fable-Fusion-711, dense 27B, uncensored/abliterated), not an official Qwen release. Now used for Open WebUI chat + custom Tools (data fetch/analysis), not coding. Tested: tool-calling works (stream+non-stream), MTP draft acceptance ~78-86%, but raw speed is only ~26 tok/s vs ~74 tok/s on qwen3.6-mtp (dense 27B costs far more per token than the sparse 35B-A3B MoE despite fewer total params). Context ceiling tested by hand: 65536 fits safely (~4.8GB headroom), 98304 triggered an internal CUDA OOM once (auto-recovered by retrying without pipeline parallelism, but left under 800MB free on one card) - not safe for real use, pinned to 65536 instead of trusting --fit's over-conservative 8192 default. Stress-tested tool-calling at temp=1.0 with a tight 400-token budget: 5/5 succeeded (unlike qwen3.6-mtp, which had real failures at its default temp before being lowered to 0.6) - so temperature was NOT overridden here, it's genuinely reliable as-is. --reasoning-budget/--no-reasoning-preserve added anyway as cheap insurance for long chat sessions, same reasoning as the coding profiles. Vision added afterward: unlike the original Unsloth qwen3.6-mtp model (whose card explicitly says MTP + --mmproj aren't supported together, why qwen3.6-main/qwen3.6-mtp are split), this DavidAU merge loads BOTH --spec-type draft-mtp and --mmproj together with no conflict - verified: vision test image correctly described AND MTP draft acceptance still ~82% simultaneously. VRAM headroom is tighter with vision loaded (~28.5GB/32GB used, ~3.8GB free) but stable, no OOM.

muse-glimmer-30b.note: Official Meta Superintelligence Lab release, dense 29.6B with a ViT-G/14 perception encoder, purpose-built for local agentic tasks - not a Qwen derivative. Needed a llama.cpp upgrade to load at all: the 'muse-glimmer' architecture wasn't recognized on b10155 (this model card's release date is Aug 2026, support merged into llama.cpp on 2026-08-10, PR #26841) - upgraded to b10355 to get it. Uses DFlash speculative decoding (block-of-16 drafter, separate --spec-draft-model file) instead of MTP, confirmed active via 'adding speculative implementation draft-dflash' in the log. Controls reasoning depth via a 'Reasoning strength: <low|medium|high|xhigh>' line in the system prompt rather than a CLI flag, so --reasoning-budget/--no-reasoning-preserve were deliberately not copied from other profiles. TESTED RESULTS: tool-calling reliable (8/8 across two batches, including a tight 400-token stress test - no reasoning-runaway issue). Vision works (mmproj loads fine alongside DFlash, no MTP-style conflict). But raw speed is only ~30-34 tok/s with DFlash active - SLOWER than qwen3.6-mtp's ~72-74 tok/s, and nowhere near the model card's claimed 3.1x/233 tok/s DFlash speedup, which was measured on an RTX 5090 (far more compute than this RTX 5060 Ti x2 setup) - marketing numbers from different hardware class did not transfer. --fit auto-picked only 8192 ctx despite ~12GB VRAM headroom being free; tested by hand instead: 131072 (matching the other main profiles) fits comfortably with ~10.3GB headroom to spare, thanks to the model's sliding-window attention (only 1 layer in 4 is 'Global', rest are 2048-window local) costing far less than Fable-Fusion's fully dense attention did. Benchmarks on the model card compare against Qwen3.6-27B specifically (not the 35B-A3B-MoE this setup actually runs day to day) with mixed results - wins agentic/tool benchmarks like MCP Atlas, loses coding-specific ones like TerminalBench/OSWorld/SWE-Bench Verified. Net: works correctly, but not faster than the current setup on this hardware - kept as a profile to try for its native tool-recovery/reasoning-strength design, not adopted as default. IMPORTANT: this profile uses Unsloth's OWN independent GGUF conversion (UD-Q4_K_XL, ~14.8GB) - see 'muse-glimmer-30b-meta' below for Meta's own official kquant-dynamic export (19.7GB), a genuinely different quantization pipeline, not the same file despite both being '4-bit-class'. [2026-09-05: added --no-reasoning-preserve after b10809 flipped its default to always-on - see README upgrade history for the reasoning.]

muse-glimmer-30b-meta.note: Meta's OWN official GGUF export (huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF) - this is the literal file the model card's 0.2%-degradation/32GB-VRAM 'K-Quant-Dynamic' claim refers to, confirmed by filename (muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-dynamic.gguf) and exact byte-size match against the repo's own listing. Different quantization pipeline from Unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL above (19.7GB vs ~14.8GB for the same nominal '4-bit' tier) - reuses the same dflash-kquant.gguf/mmproj-kquant.gguf companion files since those are byte-identical between both repos (verified via content-length before downloading only the ~18.3GB text model). TESTED HEAD-TO-HEAD vs the Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL profile above: tool-calling reliable (8/8 across two batches incl. tight-budget stress test, identical result), vision works identically ('a blue circle'), speed/draft-acceptance statistically indistinguishable (27.7-34.7 tok/s, ~54-67% acceptance vs Unsloth's 27.7-34.3 tok/s, ~54-69%) - the larger, more-precise Meta weights did NOT measurably change speed or reliability on this hardware. ctxSize 131072 hand-tested and fits, but with less headroom than Unsloth's variant (~6.8GB free vs ~10.3GB) since the weights alone are ~5GB bigger. Net: no observed practical difference between the two quantizations in this setup's actual usage (tool-calling, vision, speed) despite Meta's official 0.2% vs unknown/unverified degradation numbers - the quality gap this claims to close may only show up in evals this setup can't run, not in casual use. [2026-09-05: added --no-reasoning-preserve after b10809 flipped its default to always-on - see README upgrade history for the reasoning.]

qwen3.6-27b.note: Official Qwen (Alibaba) dense 27B, plain (no MTP) - the actual model the Muse Glimmer card's 'Qwen3.6-27B Thinking Mode' benchmark comparisons refer to, which this setup never directly tested until now (Fable-Fusion is a DavidAU uncensored merge of the same base, not the pristine original). Same sampling as qwen3.6-mtp/qwen3.6-main for direct comparability. Vision added (mmproj-F16, shared with the MTP profile - byte-identical between both Unsloth repos) and verified: correctly described the test image. [2026-09-05: added --no-reasoning-preserve after b10809 flipped its default to always-on - see README upgrade history for the reasoning.]

qwen3.6-27b-mtp.note: Official Qwen dense 27B with MTP - lets us isolate MTP's speedup contribution on a DENSE architecture (vs the sparse MoE qwen3.6-mtp) and compare against the dense+MTP Fable-Fusion merge's numbers (~26-34 tok/s, ~78-86% draft acceptance) using the pristine, uncensored-merge-free original this time. Vision added (same mmproj as qwen3.6-27b) and verified working TOGETHER with MTP (81% draft acceptance in the same vision request, no conflict) - same pleasant surprise Fable-Fusion had; only the original 35B-A3B qwen3.6-mtp documents MTP+mmproj as incompatible. [2026-09-05: added --no-reasoning-preserve after b10809 flipped its default to always-on - see README upgrade history for the reasoning.]

qwen3.8-27b-v3.note: Unsloth re-quantized this whole repo on 2026-08-19/20 with their new 'Dynamic V3.0' quantization pipeline (up from V2.0, which the original qwen3.8-27b profile above was quantized with) - same filename (Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q5_K_XL.gguf) but a genuinely different file: 20.88GB now vs 20.22GB before (confirmed via content-length, not assumed). Kept as a SEPARATE profile alongside the original V2.0 one (not replacing it, per user request) specifically to A/B compare the two pipelines head to head under identical settings/context/hardware. Reuses the existing mmproj-F16.gguf from the V2.0 folder since HF confirms that file's size is unchanged (927607488 bytes both times) - not re-downloaded. Unsloth also restructured the whole quant lineup (many more granular UD tiers: IQ1/IQ2/IQ3 variants, Q2-Q8 K_XL tiers) and, notably, added a genuine standalone MTP draft model (MTP/mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf, 1.37GB) for the first time - see qwen3.8-27b-v3-mtp below. The 'unused tensor blk.64.nextn.*' baked-in MTP head is STILL present in this V3 file too (confirmed in load log), just re-quantized at different byte sizes than V2's copy - so the old zero-download --spec-type draft-mtp trick still works here as well, V3 didn't remove it. TESTED at 131072 ctx: tool-calling 8/8 (3x generous 1024-budget + 5x tight 400-budget), vision verified (mmproj-F16 correctly described the test image), VRAM headroom ~2.3-2.9GB free per GPU (comparable to V2's ~2.1-3.5GB, the extra 0.66GB of weights barely moved the needle). Speed unaccelerated: ~16.7 tok/s - statistically the same as V2's ~16.85 tok/s, i.e. the new Dynamic V3.0 pipeline changed accuracy/quantization quality (per Unsloth's own claim of >10% better accuracy at the same size), not raw inference speed, on this hardware. Net: a like-for-like swap-in upgrade over the V2 profile with no observed downside in this setup's casual testing - the value proposition here is model quality (unverified by this setup, which doesn't run quality evals), not speed or VRAM. [2026-09-05: added --no-reasoning-preserve after b10809 flipped its default to always-on - see README upgrade history for the reasoning.]

qwen3.8-27b-v3-mtp.note: Unlike the V2.0 file (whose MTP head is baked into the main gguf as 'blk.64.nextn.*' tensors, usable via just --spec-type draft-mtp with zero download), Unsloth published this V3.0 generation's MTP drafting as a genuine standalone gguf too (MTP/mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf, 1.37GB, its own separate download) - loaded here via --spec-draft-model. --spec-type intentionally omitted so llama.cpp auto-detects the draft type from the file's own metadata (per b10430's 'auto-detect spec type from draft GGUF metadata' - see upgrade history); confirmed working via 'loading draft model' in the startup log, no errors. TESTED at 131072 ctx: tool-calling 3/3, vision verified. Speed 27-30 tok/s across two runs (comparable to qwen3.8-27b-mtp's ~28-30 tok/s using the old baked-in approach), BUT draft acceptance was noticeably more variable and lower: 63.6%-75.6% across two runs vs the baked-in V2 profile's steadier 77-79%. VRAM cost is also real and uneven here (this standalone file plus its own compute buffers landed mostly on one GPU) - only ~907MB free on GPU1 vs ~1.8-2.1GB free on both GPUs for the zero-download baked-in approach. Net: the new standalone MTP file is NOT a clear upgrade over the old zero-download trick for this quant - similar speed, worse draft acceptance, tighter VRAM margin. If running qwen3.8-27b-v3 with MTP, using --spec-type draft-mtp directly on the same v3 base file (like qwen3.8-27b-mtp does for V2) is worth trying first since it costs nothing extra to download and left more VRAM headroom in the V2 comparison - not yet tested on the V3 file specifically, but expected to behave the same way since the nextn tensors are confirmed present and unchanged in kind. [2026-09-05: added --no-reasoning-preserve after b10809 flipped its default to always-on - see README upgrade history for the reasoning.]

bonsai2-27b.note: Prism ML's Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B on MAINLINE llama.cpp (moved 2026-10-16). Mainline supports Bonsai 2 since b11669/v0.7.0 (PR #29600 adds the activation transform it needs), but only the Q2_0 packing: the PQ2_0/PTQ1_0 files from the main HF repo are fork-only types (mainline stops with 'invalid ggml type 142'). This file is prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf-dev 'Q2_0-prism-fork-required.gguf' (7.1GB, sha256 4f99aed0...), renamed. Before b11669 mainline would load it and print gibberish with no warning, so do not use it on an older build. mmproj copied from the fork's models folder. Same settings as the fork profile (one GPU: --device CUDA1, GPU0 left free for Video Studio). TESTED 2026-10-16 on b11669: bench/validate.py tool call, streamed call, tool loop, vision all OK; 12/12 tool calls with thinking off, none returned slashes (PrismML #342 does not apply here); English and Thai text coherent. Versus the fork on the same tests: decode 37.4 vs 40.7 tok/s (-8%), GPU1 13.2 vs 12.3 GB VRAM, load 47s. The fork profile is kept as bonsai2-27b-prism. Sampling from the model card (thinking mode, min_p=0.05); the template accepts reasoning effort xhigh/medium/low, 'high' returns HTTP 500.

bonsai2-27b-prism.note: FALLBACK (2026-10-16): the original profile on the PrismML fork, kept in case mainline regresses; bonsai2-27b now runs mainline. Prism ML's Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B (Qwen3.8-27B with ternary {-1,0,+1} weights, 1.72 bits/weight, PQ2_0 pack = 7.2GB vs 20.9GB for the Q5_K_XL the qwen3.8-27b-v3 profile uses). Stock llama.cpp cannot run these files (it rejects the PQ2_0/PTQ1_0 types), so this profile sets its own llamaDir/modelsDir pointing at a separate install of the PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp fork (C:\llama.cpp-prism, release prism-b10754-2459f68, win-cuda-13.3 build) - C:\llama.cpp is untouched and the fork does not upgrade with it; update it separately from github.com/PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp/releases. Runs on ONE GPU by design (--device CUDA1 plus --mmproj-device CUDA1, the card with no display attached): ~12.4GB used at 131072 ctx with vision loaded, ~3.8GB free on that card, GPU0 left entirely free. Loads in ~15s. Sampling from the model card (thinking mode, min_p=0.05). Template defaults to xhigh reasoning effort; the card says 'high' returns HTTP 500 and 'low' behaves like xhigh, so only xhigh/medium are usable. TESTED 2026-10-03 through the control server on port 11435: tool-calling 8/8 (3x 1024-budget + 5x 400-budget), streamed tool call assembles into valid JSON with finish_reason tool_calls, a 3-step tool loop (read_file -> get_weather -> final answer) completed correctly, vision correct, ~42 tok/s (vs ~17 for qwen3.8-27b-v3 unaccelerated, ~74 for qwen3.6-mtp). NOT verified: answer quality (the vendor's '98.2% of FP16' figure is their own measurement; this setup has no eval harness) and long agentic sessions - the vendor's KNOWN_ISSUES.md lists malformed/looping tool calls as an open model limitation.

saluki-27b.note: ConwayResearch/Underdog-Saluki-27B-1.0: Qwen3.8-27B squeezed to 7.89GB (IQ2-mix, ~2.3 bits/weight, built on ISTA-DASLab's GSQ-RCO quant) and tuned to keep tool calling intact. Unlike bonsai2-27b it is a standard GGUF, so it runs on the stock C:\llama.cpp build. Runs on ONE GPU like bonsai2-27b (--device CUDA1, the card without the display). Sampling from the model card for thinking mode (temp 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20); the card suggests thinking off + temp 0 for fast direct tool calls. Vision via the card's Q8_0 mmproj. See README for the 3-way benchmark against qwen3.8-27b-v3 and bonsai2-27b.

qwen3.8-27b-bartowski.note: bartowski/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF Q5_K_M (20.92GB, imatrix, his re-uploaded 2026-09-11 tensor layout). Same size as Unsloth's UD-Q5_K_XL in qwen3.8-27b-v3, so the two isolate the quantization recipe. Settings identical to qwen3.8-27b-v3. Added 2026-10-12 for the quantizer comparison in README.

qwen3.8-27b-ggml-org.note: ggml-org/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF Q4_K_M (18.97GB), the llama.cpp team's own conversion: the closest thing to an official GGUF (Qwen only publishes safetensors). Settings identical to qwen3.8-27b-v3. Added 2026-10-12 for the quantizer comparison in README.

qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4.note: cdiamond/Qwen3.8-27B-iMatrix-NVFP4-MTP-GGUF (17.13GB, 5.01 bpw): mostly NVFP4 (Blackwell-native FP4, which the RTX 5060 Ti supports) with Q5_K/Q6_K/Q8_0 on the sensitive tensors, chosen with an imatrix from agent sessions. Embedded MTP head. Settings identical to qwen3.8-27b-v3. Added 2026-10-12 for the quantizer comparison in README.

qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4-mtp.note: Same file as qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4, with its embedded MTP head used for speculative decoding (--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2, the same draft depth as the other MTP profiles). Added 2026-10-13. [2026-10-16, b11669: added --spec-draft-n-ubatch 128 (MTP draft context batch; default = -ub 512). Sweep 0/256/128/64 at 8k/32k prompts: VRAM GPU1 13394/13036/12858/12768 MiB, commit 36.5/35.9/35.6/35.4 GB, prefill and decode within noise down to 128; 64 started to slow at 32k (prefill 1026 vs ~1060, decode 24.4 vs ~27). 128 saves ~0.5 GB VRAM and ~0.9 GB commit for free.]
